subject: Multi-level filters - reactive order not optimal

messages.author: 6f9739ea511c7a89
messages.subject: Multi-level filters - reactive order not optimal
parts:
I'm having issues with multi-level filters (one filter dependent on another), causing render functions to run multiple times when it should only run once.  This is particularly painful since renderGvis crashes when too much happens at once.

I came up with a hacky solution that works, but I don't like it.  There MUST be a better way to do this.  No?

DETAILS
  • Setup: I have a gVis that is dependent on a reactive dataset().  That dataset() is dependent on two dynamic renderUI inputs.  One of those inputs, inputB, is dependent on inputA.
  • I want this to happen: user updates inputA, then inputB reacts to that, which updates dataset() with the new inputA and inputB, and the gVis refreshes based on the new dataset().  
  • But this is happening: user updates inputA, which updates dataset() and refreshes the gVis; then inputB updates based on inputA, which updates dataset() again, which refreshes the gvis one more time.
  • Problem: If you have used gVis, you know it could be finicky sometimes if things happen too fast.  In this case, gvis is getting updated twice in really short time, causing the charts to disappear. Not to mention the code is less efficient if it runs gvis twice when it only needs to run once.
  • Hacky solution: isolate dataset() from the renderGvis.  Make that renderGvis only reactive to inputB

SIMPLIFIED VERSION OF THE CODE
(pardon typos; the code works; I sanitized it heavily for sake of example)

## filter() is from dplyr package

output$inputA_categories <- renderUI({
  categories <- unique(raw_data()$category)
  selectInput("inputA", "Select Category", categories, categories)
})
output$inputB_clients <- renderUI({
  data <- filter(raw_data(), category == input$inputA)
  clients <- unique(data$client)
  checkboxGroupInput("inputB", "Client filter", clients, clients)
})

dataset <- reactive({
      # i do need to filter both category and client.  since clients cover different categories, i can't just filter client
      dataset <- filter(raw_data(), category == input$inputA, client == input$inputB)
      [many other operations removed for simplicity]

      return(dataset)
})

output$barcharts <- renderGvis({
    # hack that works: want to update gvis only when input B is updated
    input$inputB

    # hack that works: isolate dataset() so gvis doesn't refresh when dataset() is only partially updated with inputA but not inputB.  
    isolate( {
      if(is.null(dataset())) return(NULL)
      gvisBarChart(data=dataset(), xvar=.., yvar=..)
    })
  })
